title: Atlanta social media influencer indicted in $4 million SNAP fraud scheme - WABE

Atlanta influencer Shawty Dred indicted in SNAP fraud scheme

 Atlanta social media influencer indicted in $4 million SNAP fraud scheme

 SNAP 
 Atlanta social media influencer indicted in $4 million SNAP fraud scheme
 Crime 
 Kendall Murry 
 | WABE 
 October 22nd, 2026
 A SNAP EBT information sign is displayed at a gas station in Riverwoods, Ill., Nov. 1, 2025. (AP Photo/Nam Y. Huh, File) 
 The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia announced Wednesday that social media personality Mercedes Reshard New, also known as “Shawty Dred,” has been arrested on federal charges after obtaining more than $4 million in fraudulent SNAP benefits.
 SNAP, a federal program administered by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), provides monthly benefits to low-income households to pay for food. The office has accused New of using the illegal funds to “bankroll a life of luxury.”
 “New allegedly stole over $4 million meant for poor families who need help putting food on the table,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg in a Wednesday press release. “My office is fully committed to rooting out abuses of the SNAP program and holding accountable criminal con artists and scammers who appallingly seek to profit by stealing taxpayer money meant to feed vulnerable Americans.”
 How did New commit SNAP fraud?
 According to the release, New allegedly held control of more than 350 fraudulent SNAP accounts between January 2020 and July 2026.
 These accounts, created using stolen identities, allegedly allowed New to have SNAP EBT debit cards mailed across various metro Atlanta addresses and to apply for his limited liability company, Shawty Dred LLC, to become an authorized SNAP retailer. 
 Between April 2024 and November 2025, the social media personality allegedly began to use fraudulently obtained EBT debit cards and a point-of-sale device associated with Shawty Dred LLC to swipe SNAP benefits totaling more than $660,000. 
 In November 2025, USDA officials revoked New’s store authorization, and local police officers arrested the influencer approximately two weeks later for allegedly selling SNAP benefits at a metro Atlanta store. 
 Officers seized 14 EBT debit cards from New, all issued to other people, during the arrest.
 A federal grand jury indicted New on 46 counts of mail fraud, 15 counts of aggravated identity theft, and one count each of SNAP fraud and illegal transactions with access devices on October 7, 2026. He was later arrested on Oct. 13 and remains in U.S. Marshals Service custody pending further proceedings.
 What did New spend the illegally obtained SNAP funds on?
 According to officials, New used the fraudulent money he obtained to fund and show off his extravagant lifestyle on social media.
 On his Instagram account, richlifeshawtydred, various posts show the social media personality flying on private jets, posing with ultra-luxury Rolls-Royce and Maybach vehicles.
 “Mr. ‘Shawty Dred’ allegedly stole food assistance benefits in Georgia from the poorest Americans. He then flaunted his luxurious living off fraudulent proceeds on Instagram and TikTok like there’s nothing ‘New’ under the sun,” said USDA Inspector General John Walk in the release.  
 “But in alignment with the leaderships of VP Vance and the WH Task Force on Fraud, we don’t look the other way when fraudsters get rich off exploiting poverty and cheat the compassion of American taxpayers.”
 The U.S. Department of Agriculture Office of Inspector General and the Federal Bureau of Investigation are investigating this case, with valuable assistance from the Georgia Department of Human Services Office of Inspector General.
